prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Lowering the density-weight growth aggressiveness in the overflow-based update (clamping `density_weight_new` to a smaller max and slowing the step-size growth) keeps the analytical placement in a less-congested regime with more whitespace around critical logic, so the single fixed timing-repair pass can insert buffers and shorten detours, reducing TNS across all circuits.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.188 robust(mean-std)=-0.007 min_case=-0.028 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.076 dWNS=+4.6% dTNS=+9.5% overflow~132
  bp-ng45: score=+0.141 dWNS=+1.8% dTNS=+22.2% overflow~91
  bp_fe-ng45: score=-0.028 dWNS=-1.4% dTNS=-3.8% overflow~118
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis only partly holds. Two of three cases improved (ariane133-ng45: dTNS +9.5%, dWNS +4.6%; bp-ng45: dTNS +22.2%), consistent with more whitespace easing buffer insertion. But bp_fe-ng45 regressed (dTNS -3.8%, dWNS -1.4%), and the robust mean-std is slightly negative (-0.007), so the gain isn't uniform. Next step: sweep the density-weight cap per circuit family, or make the growth rate adaptive to overflow magnitude, to avoid the bp_fe regression while retaining the ariane/bp gains.
